cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set G1 for the full 2026-27 year: in-state tuition $6,930, out-of-state and nonresident tuition $18,600, required fees $410, on-campus food and housing $19,552 (the CDS names The Towers co-ed residence hall). International (F-1/J-1) students pay the nonresident rate. Estimated expenses (G5): books and supplies $1,500; other expenses $6,283 for residents and for commuters not living at home, $3,227 for commuters living at home; commuters not living at home food and housing $23,022; transportation is blank. Per-credit-hour charges: $305 in-state, $620 nonresident. CDS H6 ticks only that institutional non-need-based scholarship and grant aid is available to degree-seeking nonresidents (institutional need-based aid is not ticked); the recipient count and average award are left blank.

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set 2025-2026 (Fall 2025 entering class; PDF updated July 2026): 34,284 applied, 19,880 admitted (58.0%), 2,700 enrolled; the men and women rows and the residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international) each add up to those totals. International (nonresident) first-years: 1,170 applied, 317 admitted (27%), 127 enrolled. No early decision or early action, and no waitlist (C2 answered No). The CDS leaves the SAT/ACT submit rates and percentiles (C9) blank, so the SAT percentiles shown and the 11% SAT submit rate (271 students) are College Navigator (IPEDS) figures for fall 2024; no ACT percentiles are listed. The CDS reports an average high school GPA of 3.14 for the 92% who gave a GPA; its C11 GPA-range table is filled in only for 'students who submitted scores' (the all-students and non-submitter columns read 0.00), so no distribution is shown. Undergraduate enrollment (14,379) is the B2 total and the nonresident count (577) the B2 'Total Undergraduates' nonresident cell (fall 2025); student-to-faculty ratio is CDS I-2 (14 to 1).

cds_test_policy.notes: From the Common Data Set C8: SAT or ACT 'not required for admission, but considered if submitted'. CCNY's freshman page lists 'SAT or ACT scores (if submitted)' among the review factors.
